the Buddha, in the 2d or 3d week after enlightenment, (dvitīye) saptāhe tathāgato dīrghacaṅkramaṃ caṅkramyate sma, (tṛtīyaṃ) saptāhaṃ prītisukhena dīrghaṃ caṅkramaṃ caṅkrame (aor.); (Buddha, vihārāto nirgamya … smitaṃ prāduṣkaritvā) dīrghaṃ caṅkramaṃ caṅkrame (aor.); (All remaining citations in this article are from verses.) caryā may be used even in vss, where meter is indifferent (so) or requires long first syllable (), tho in the latter case cāri (˚ī) and cārikā, qq.v., are also found; nearly all the cases here cited refer to the religious course leading to enlightenment, to Buddhahood or Bodhisattvahood, but occasionally the term is applied to any or all human courses of action, including such as are disapproved; iya bāla-carī, this foolish (or childish) course (vs); jāniya te cariṃ ca, knowing them (all the creatures of the world) and their (various) course(s) of action; cariṃcariṃ jāniya nityakālaṃ vadāmi sattvāna tathā-tathāhaṃ, knowing the various modes of conduct (of beings) always, I speak to creatures in this or that way (,, cari acari, metrically impossible, and uninterpretable; the moving and not-moving [of living beings], which seems unacceptable); jagataḥ prajānase yā carir yatha ca karmasaṃbhavaḥ; otherwise, referring to the course of Bodhisattvas, also called the true (bhūta), subtle (sūkṣma), pure (viśuddha), supreme (uttama) course, the course of (leading to) enlightenment (bodhi-), of morality (śīla-), or other similar epithets; also duṣkara-, referring to Śākyamuniʼs temporary experiment with severe austerities; often former, ancient (pūrva, purima) with allusion to the length of it thru many past births; frequently a form of the cognate verb car (also ā-car) is used with it: sūkṣmāṃ cariṃ; (= Pali cetasika); in the following cait˚ is written except in the passages listed s.v. cet˚; mental, of the mind: often contrasted with kāyika, sometimes also with vācika; sarvakāyika-caitasika-prapīḍitāny; kāyika-caitasikaṃ … sukhaṃ; kāyikaṃ caitasikaṃ (sc. sukham); cetasikena (parallel to kāyikena and vācikena) sthāmena; kāyikaṃ ca me duḥkhaṃ cetasikaṃ ca; kāyikāḥ klamāḥ caitasikāḥ (so!) apy upāyāsāḥ; without such contrasting words, ˚kī (sc. vedanā); caitasikenābhyāsena; cittāni caitasika-saṃjñi (acc. pl. of -saṃjñā) vitarkitāni; esp. with dharma, regularly pl., mental states or conditions of existence, ˚kā dharmāḥ; read cetasikā in (ye … dharmā pratītya utpadyante, [Page233-b] so substantially with mss., …) te … cetasikā (vedayitā; mss. in 14 cetasitā or ˚yitā, one ms. in 7 veṭayitā); na cittaṃ na cetasikā dharmāḥ, there is no mind, no mental states of existence; cittacaitasikānām eva dharmāṇām, and ˚kā dharmāḥ 5, apparently the mindʼs mental states, states that are mental as belonging to the mind (?), cf. Pali citta-cetasikā dhammā, Dhammasaṅgaṇi But in other occurrences of both together, in Pali and BHS, cittam and caitasikā dharmāḥ (cetasikā dhammā), or caitasika (usually masc. pl.) with dh˚ understood, constitute a duality, the mind and mental states-of-being. (For Pali see e.g. cittacetasikānaṃ samaṃ sammā ca ādhānaṃ; mind and mental properties, Maung Tin.) Cf., above, and: kuśalānāṃ ca citta-caitasikānām (so read) anusmṛtir, remembrance of meritorious mind and mental states. In kīdṛśās te cittacetasikāḥ (certainly sc. dharmāḥ) pravartante, kliṣṭā vākliṣṭā vā, and similarly in the sequel, the cpd. may perhaps be a Tatp., mental states of the mind, rather than a dvandva. On the other hand cf., comm., marīcikopamau dvau dharmau, cittaṃ caitasikāś ca; here the duality is obvious, and dharmāḥ is certainly to be supplied with cait˚. In the usual equivalent is caitta, q.v.; note that the word dharma regularly has to be supplied, or at least is not expressed, but note avasthāviśeṣo 'pi hi nāma cetasaś caitasiko bhavati (is dharmaḥ here also to be supplied with the masc. quasi-subst. caitasiko ?). As in above, they are false, delusive, illusory.

(= Pali codeti), accuses (a person, acc., of an offense, instr.): pudgalaṃ … āpattyā codayiṣyāmo (so Pali āpattiyā codeti, accuses of sin); taṃ vaidyu vijño na mṛṣeṇa codayet, a wise man would not accuse that physician of lying; in very common with smārayati, e.g. ced … codayeyaṃ smārayeyaṃ, if I should accuse and warn …; a necessary preliminary to suspension, ib.. See saṃcodayati.

(nt.; not recorded in this sense), stealth, in the sense of secrecy: (ya imaṃ dharmaparyāyaṃ …) rahasi cauryeṇāpi kasyacid … saṃprakāśayed (prose), who should declare this dharma-paryāya even by stealth in secret to anyone …

, falls (to a lower existence); in Skt. and, so far as I have found, in Pali (cavati) construed with abl. of the existence departed from; here sometimes with loc. instead, dies, passes away in …: cyutvā manuṣyeṣu avīci teṣāṃ pratiṣṭha bhotī paripūrṇakalpān, (4) … cyutāś ca tatra prapatanti (and with ms. Ḱ cyutāś-cyutās tatra patanti) bālāḥ, (5) yadā ca narakeṣu (˚kebhya) cyutā bhavanti …, having fallen (from existence, i.e. having died) among men, Avīci becomes their abode for full kalpas … and having fallen (died) there, the fools fall (lower); and when they come to fall (die) in (Kashgar, from) the hells …
(= Pali cutūpapāta), fall (from one existence) and rebirth (in another), see s.v. upapāda.

(nt.; = Pali id., and; only chakana reported in Pali literature; = Skt. śakṛt), dung: in (vs) read chaka-mūtram eva sṛjaṃ (= sṛjan, pres. pple.) for charda-gūtham … (mss. chada-mūrtam, or chanda-mūrtem); my reading is proved by the corresponding prose uccāra-prasrāvaṃ muñcamāno.
, perhaps to be understood instead of śaṭa-, q.v., in. Cf. next.

(Skt. chaṭā, AMg. chaḍā; āmreḍita), mass; instr. adv., in a mass, French en masse: taṃ tālaskandhaṃ pṛthivīye chaṭāchaṭāye (in one great mass;, lourdement) upari patitaṃ; tāni bandhanāni hastena chaṭachaṭāya (in one single mass, en masse; = all with one stroke) chindati. Both prose.
(= Pali id.) abandons: ˚ti;; mss. corrupt in both, but context makes ʼs em. seem certain; in the only ms. choḍḍeti (lacuna in other ms.).

, acc. to Tib. sgo ḥu chuṅ, app. small door, or ske ḥu (? ske = neck), in ˚kā-vārika, some servant or official in a monastery; Chin. and Jap. watcher at a small gate or door, app. agreeing with the first Tib. gloss.

, nt., and ˚ikā, f. (both Skt. Lex.; cf. Pali ahi-chattaka, nt., mushroom), mushroom: tad yathā chattrakaṃ (mss.; em. chā˚) evaṃ varṇapratibhāso pi abhūṣi; same phrase has in mss. vāḍakam, em. chātrakaṃ; chattrikāṃ.

, corrupt reading in for; read cipiṭaṃ, flat (agreeing with nāsa in next line), with, supported by Tib. sna leb, flat nose. The mss. cited by vary greatly and at random. and both translate as if they read cipiṭaṃ.]

for -channa (Skt.), covered, in (text) ducchanaṃ and succhanaṃ, yathā hy agāraṃ du˚ and … su˚ 17—22; meter favors, indeed almost demands, channaṃ, which is read in the same vss in Pali,, and must, it seems, be adopted here, tho the manifold repetition of this obvious error is strange.

, (1) m. (rarely nt.,), = Skt. and Pali id., used in both bad and good sense; more often in bad, desire, whim, caprice, passion, see e.g. acchandagāmin; in good sense, zeal, a characteristic of a Bodhisattva or a Buddha; often associated with vīrya: asti me (sc. Bodhisattvasya) chando 'sti vīryaṃ, same passage as: mahyaṃ pi khalu asti chando …; asti chandaṃ (n. sg.! one ms. ˚as) tathā vīryaṃ = asti chando ca vīryaṃ ca (vs; note chandaś ca, just above); nāsti chandasya hāniḥ (one of the 18 āveṇika Buddha-dharma); (āryasmitaṃ, of the Bodhisattva) chandopastabdhaṃ, based on zeal; janemi chandaṃ; (2) (m.; this mg. in Pali, see s.v. 2), approval, consent, as object of dā-, give: dadāti … tathāgataś chandam …, the Tathāgata (who sends this message; not Śākyamuni; neither nor understands the passage) gives his consent (to the opening of this stūpa); chandārhibhyaś [Page235-a] (= Pali chandāraha, see esp., one who has the right to a valid vote) ca chandenānītā bhavanti (are agreed in consenting); (3) n. of Buddhaʼs charioteer, oftener called Chandaka (4), q.v.:;; both times in vss, the -ka possibly dropped m.c., cf. (note that Chandaka is the form used in prose two lines before in); but in (prose) also Chanda, = Pali Channa, assumed in to be this same person; here as in subjected to utkṣepaṇīya;; the corresponding name in Pali is Channa; (4) n. of one of the ṣaḍvārgika monks:.

, (1) nt. (= Pali id.; from chanda plus ka; see also chanda-yācaka), ‘free-will offering’, general collection of alms for the community of monks, made by going the rounds of the town and inviting subscriptions from all citizens ( describes this); chandakāni; otherwise only chandaka-bhikṣaṇa (nt.) in same mg.,;;;;;;; in (see) read chandaka-(ed. chandana)-bhikṣaṇa (ms. and ed. bhikṣa; but the missing -ṇa is read in line 7 below); (2) in … indriyair avikalatvasya kuśaladharmachandakasya āścaryādbhuto loke prādurbhāvaḥ,, renders -chandaka by gathering (of merit); but cf. Pali dhamma-chanda, desire for the Law, opp. to kāmachanda, desire for lusts; this is certainly the word involved; either chandaka = chanda (ka svārthe), or, perhaps better, read -chandatvasya, which matches the preceding series of nouns in -tva-sya, the appearance in the world of a state of desiring meritorious (or, felicitous) dharma (Law, or states of being ?) is a prodigious marvel; (3) in text tīvreṇa chandakaḥ, presumably adj., desiring (vehemently); but v.l. chandena, and so without v.l. (also Index of Kyoto ed. lists this reference under chanda, not under chandaka); this is prob. the true reading: with vehement desire (chanda); (4) n. of the Bodhisattvaʼs charioteer (in Pali Channa; here rarely Chanda, q.v.); sometimes even when the meter seems to demand Chanda, Chandaka is written, as in; this is the regular form in prose and vs; (prose), 6, 9;; (prose); (prose);;;;;;;;;;;; sent with Kālodāyin by Śuddhodana as messenger to Buddha after his enlightenment,
, nt. (see prec.), n. of a caitya built on the spot where Chandaka left the Bodhisattva as he gave up wordly life:.
, adj. with bhikṣu, monk begging for the chandaka (-bhikṣaṇa), q.v.: ˚kā (bhikṣavaḥ).

(from Skt. chandas plus -vin; sc. vidyā ?), metrics, versification: ˚vinyāṃ (prose; so nearly all mss., v.l. chandasi nyāya-; … bodhisattva eva viśiṣyate sma); Tib. tshig (word) sdeb pa (combining; also to make poetry, to compose verses,).
, m. (= Pali chandāraha), see s.v. chanda (2).

(from chanda plus -ika; = Pali id., not well defined, cf. a-cchandika), desirous, with instr., inf., at end of cpds., or without complement: parasmai cārthikāya chandikāya kulaputrāya … yācamānāya; chandiko bhaviṣyati … lekhayitum; (buddhaguṇebhiḥ) (vs); bhūyaś-chandika, desiring more, greedy,; ˚ka-tā, abstr., in tīvra-cch˚, kuśala- 8.
, adj., (garment) with hidden fringe or border, forbidden to monks:; prob. corruption for Pali acchinnadasa, in corresp. passage; see -daśaka.

(= Pali chambhati, perhaps to be read here; derivs. of this root are spelled with b, not bh, in this text; see also sa-cchambita; cf. the next entries, and (ac)chambhin, (ac)chambhita(tva)), is frightened: bibhety api chambaty apy uttrasaty api,,. The MIndic chambhati is clearly based on Skt. skambh-; BHS (rarely) uses the equivalent stambh- in the same sense, see astambhin.
, nt. (= chambh˚, see prec.), state of being frightened: Dhvajāgrasūtra (as prec.),.
, adj. (ppp., cf. prec. entries and next, also acchambhita; Pali id., for Skt. *skambhita = BHS stambh-,, cf. a-stambhin), frightened: ˚to.
, see chambin and acchambhin, and cf. astambhin.

, text in kola-challaṃ pi āhāram āharanti; so one ms., but v.l. kolaṃ curṇṇa, which clearly points to kola-cūrṇaṃ = Pali kola-cuṇṇaṃ, in a closely parallel passage; so read; powder of jujube-berries. assumes a m. or nt. equivalent of challi, bark (Pali, late and lex. Skt., see.)]

, adj. (also śava, q.v.; Pali chava, homonymous with chava = Skt. śava, corpse, and perhaps ultimately the same word, cf.,), base, vile, wretched: śūrāṃ sāhasikāṃ chavāṃ (acc. pl.); pattrāhāro chavāvāsī, having a wretched dwelling.

(= Skt., Pali id., skin), bark (of a tree): kovidārasya chavigandhaḥ (prose). Acc. to the English of, chavi may have this mg. in AMg.; this is a translation of Hindi chāl, which seems to mean both skin and bark; whether the AMg. word also means bark I do not know.
, adj. (to Skt. ˚la), of a goat: ˚ka dṛti, goatskin bag,.

, adj., thin; occurs, tho rarely, in Skt., as well as Pkt. chāa, cf., with comm.;;; acc. to, Pali chāta, Pkt. chāa, hungry, is an unrelated word, from *psāta, while our chāta is from *kṣāta; this theory seems speculative. In = = (vs) em. cāpodare, but read chātodare with all mss. in first and third citations (in second nābhodare); cf. chātodarī in comm. to, above; also kṣudhā chātatarodarīm.)
, ifc. (cf. Skt. chādana etc.; this stem seems not recorded anywhere), cover, protection: tad rājyaṃ dharma-chādaṃ (with dharma as its protection) prādāt (prose).

, Skt., (1) covers: in, text, kuñjaraṃ pi so … ṣaṣṭihāyanaṃ balaśaktikāye chāditavyaṃ manyeya, yo me … ṣaḍ vābhijñā balaṃ (so mss.) vaśībhāvaṃ chādayitavyaṃ manyeyā (the last part, from yo …, repeated 6—7, 8, 9—10). For the first chāditavyaṃ, thinks a form of chaḍḍeti must be read; but the Pali parallel reads tālapattikāya chādetabbaṃ, (an elephant) to be covered with a palm-leaf, which proves chāditavyaṃ correct. Perhaps read before it (with the Pali) tāla-pattrikāye; possibly, however, tala-śaktikāye (closer to our mss.), with an upheld arm or hand, see s.v. talaśaktikā. (2) protects, helps, saves (cf. s.v. 6, schützen): in (vs) read, kṛpakaruṇā janiyā atiraudre chāditu so bho (so best ms. A; all other mss. and Calc. śobhe, which [Page236-a] is uninterpretable), (by you) taking pity and compassion on your very cruel (foe), he, lo! was protected (helped). So Tib. seems clearly to read; it ends, de ni (that very one) khyod kyis (by you) bskyabs (protect, help)).

, m., and chāyā (see also duśchāya, ˚yā, mahāchāyā), a kind of evil supernatural being, acc. to Tib. on chāyā = grib gnon, harpy, a demon that defiles and poisons food; fem. also;, etc.; masc., na chāyaḥ chāyasamatīye sthānaṃ.

, nt., or ˚kā, f. (cf. Pali chārikā; AMg. chāria, ˚ya, nt., and ˚yā; no form with y for r recorded), ashes: chāyikam (so Index; text, also, chayikam; short a seems clearly an error) api na prajñāyate (Tib. thal ba, dust, ashes; follows maśīr, or maśir, q.v., api …); (na maṣir) na chāyikā prajñāyate; in (vs) read, substantially with mss., na … maṣī (mss. add va; read vā? or na?) chāyikā (mss. chā-ikā, or chāyi; em. chārikāṃ) vā (the first part of the line is corrupt but ʼs em. cannot be right; the negative was clearly present); one of four vikṛta-bhojana, chāyikā. See also jambū-chāyaka.
(acc. sg. ˚ṭim), in kāñjikacchiṭim, an inferior kind of sour gruel (kāñjika):. Replaced by simple kāñjikam in lines 15, 21, 26.
(suggests reading Chibbāsuta; I find no trace of anything like either), n. of a nāga;.

(nt.;), all manner of holes: (na svapet) chidrāchidreṣu sattvānāṃ yac ca sthānaṃ mahadbhayam (mahābh˚), cited (one should not sleep) in all manner of holes of creatures (animals), and (not in) whatever is a place of great danger. Both translations are incorrect.
(nt.; to next), in a-cchid˚, the (not) making defective: ˚raṇāvipādanatayā (i.e. -avipād˚).
(cf. prec. and next; to Skt. chidra with kṛ-), makes defective: -samādānaṃ na chidrīkaroti (bodhisattvaḥ).
(m.; to prec.) = ˚karaṇa; in cpd.,.
, adj. (ppp.; not recorded in this sense), wearied; in strī-, bhāra-, mārga-chinna,;; Tib. dub pa.

, adj. (Bhvr.; = Pali ˚bhatta), or ˚taka, with food cut off, fasting, not having eaten: brāhmaṇaś chinnabhakto (having had no breakfast) halaṃ vāhayati; (same phrase, ˚ktako). See also bhakta-chinnaka.
, one who has fallen away from observance of the rainy season: (Tib. dbyar gnas pa las ñams pa); also varṣā-chinnaka (spelled varṣācchi˚);.

, adj. or subst. nt. (also chuṭī; cf. Skt. root chuṭ-; perh. read chuṭṭha ? cf. In parallels sphuṭa (q.v., 2); read so ?
, adj. (Jain Skt. and Pali, clever; also Pali good,, comm. sundara, opp. pāpaka, of odors), good, proper, seemly: na chekaṃ na pratirūpaṃ.

[Page236-b] cutter (of wood ? quite uncertain): nāpitā (v.l. nāvikā) kalpikā chedakā (v.l. chedakārakā) lepakā sthapati-; by em. also in (nāpitā, v.l. nāvikā) kalpikā (mss. ˚akā) che˚ (but mss. chādakā) lepakā sthapati-. (also cheda; in this sense not recorded; Pali has chejja-bhejja-,, and chejjā, fem., alone,, only as forms of punishment; inaccurate), always associated with bhedya; both in lists of military arts, usually as mastered by the young Bodhisattva or another young prince; precise mg. is never made clear; Tib. on and on renders chedya by bcad pa, cutting, and bhedya by dral ba, splitting, tearing asunder: chedyam, bhedyam; otherwise only in loc., usually listed with other martial arts, chedye and bhedye, and (here chede, bhede, and so v.l. elsewhere in; the young Bodhisattva challenges other Śākya youths to test their skill in such arts);;;;;.

, rarely () choḍ˚ (cf. prec.; not in Pali; AMg. and JM. ppp. choḍi(y)a, discharged, released; Hindi choṛnā, let go, release, abandon, etc., see s.v. choṛnu), (1) clears away, removes: (withered flowers from caityas) choretva jālaṃ (see jāla) jinacetiyeṣu; (vss); same passages choritva, but 6, 8, 10 apanīya (ms.; wrongly em. to upa˚ in ed.); Tib. cited by as bsal ba, which can only mean remove, clear away; immediately following verses deal unambiguously with meritorious clearing away of withered flowers, and in choretva is again used, with objects osannapuṣpaṃ and nirmālyaṃ; and misunderstand; pātrādhiṣṭhānaṃ chorayitavyam, he must put away the (food-)bowl-stand; (2) throws away (refuse, food-leavings, dirty water, etc.): chorayiṣyāmaḥ = (water with which the food bowl has been washed); (leavings of food); ekānte chorayitvā (id.; text sthor˚); chorito (food regarded as unclean); annapānaṃ choryate; ucchiṣṭodakaṃ choritaṃ; tad (foul stuff) ekānte chorayitvā; chorayitvā (a dead body); sapta parvatā utpāṭitā, utpāṭayitvā laghunīvānyapradeśe chorayitvā, having plucked up and thrown away; with gen., tasya pātraśeṣaṃ ˚yanti, threw to that (ape) what (food) was left in their bowls; (3) discharges (bodily discharges): chorayiṣyāmaḥ (˚mi; not in an improper place); emits (a sigh), ucchvāsaṃ choritam; (4) casts off, puts aside, lays down (garments, ornaments): vastrāṇy ābharaṇāni ca pṛthivyāṃ chorayanti sma; mukuṭaṃ … chorayitvā (vs), (Śuddhodana) laying off his diadem (etc., in saluting the Bodhisattva); (5) abandons, leaves (a place): choritva kṣetrāṇi svaka-svakāni (vs), leaving their several (Buddha-)fields (they have come here; misunderstood by and); kva tvaṃ gato 'si mama śayi chorayitvā (vs; Gopā apostrophizes the Bodhisattva), abandoning my bed; (6) abandons, gives up: rājyaṃ ca rāṣṭraṃ ca chorayitvā = (vs); choritā (? precise mg. uncertain from lack of context); gives away (in largess), paṭakāś choritāḥ; (7) abandons, deserts (a person): taṃ (sc. rājānaṃ) choḍitvā (v.l. choḍayitvā) (prose); choritaḥ (a man);; chorayantu (a woman, in a cemetery, after cutting off her hands, feet, ears, and nose); sa tam ekānte prakramya (read prakrāmya? [Page237-a] caus.) chorayitvā prakrāntaḥ (em. violently), making him go off to one side and deserting him, he departed; (8) gets rid of, relieves oneself of (periods of life in the world): iyataḥ Subhūte kalpān bodhisattvo … [Page237-b] chorayati vipṛṣṭhīkaroti saṃsārād vyantīkaroti, so many aeons the Bodhisattva gets rid of, abandons, puts an end to, from the round of existence (i.e. he shortens his necessary stay in the saṃsāra).
(semi-MIndic for Skt. yakṛt; cf. AMg. jagaya), liver: (vs; v.l. ya˚).
, nt., n. of a kind of magic gem: ˚bhaṃ nāma mahāmaṇiratnaṃ.
, m. (Skt. Lex. and Pali id., acc. to nt., which its citations do not prove; jaṅgalāni is an adj.), wild place, jungle: khānayet kūpa jaṅgale (vs); ujjaṅgalo ca jaṅgalo (treated as n. pr. by).
, n. of a (tantalizing) state of preta-existence:.
, n. of a monk:;. Neither the name, nor the story told of him, seems to be associated with any of the Pali Kassapas.
, nt. (cf. Pali ˚pesanika, ˚ṇika, running errands on foot), ‘foot-errand’, the sending (someone) on foot on an errand: nāsti taj jaṅghāpreṣaṇaṃ yan notsahate.
(m.; = Pali id., ‘usually in phrase ˚raṃ anucaṅkamati anuvicarati’,), walk, stroll (on foot): ˚ram anucaṅkramyamāṇo; ˚ram anukrāmati.
, nt., the ceremony of clipping a young boyʼs hair except for the top-knot: (Rāhulasya) ˚karma; = Skt. cūḍākaraṇa, which replaces this as exact synonym in line 18 below.
, n. of a śreṣṭhin and medical authority:;
, n. of a village chiefʼs daughter:.
, n. of a local ruler (pradeśarājan), previous incarnation of Devadatta:.
(var. ˚pāra), some sort of herb: = Tib. zur ba (not recorded in Dictt.).

, loc. ˚tre, lit. lac-machine, n. of some art, in a list of those in which the Bodhisattva excelled; so read in, for jala-yantre; mss. vary, A (the best) cited as janu- (read jatu-)y˚; Calc. jatu˚, confirmed by Tib. rgya skyegs kyi ḥkhrul ḥkhor, machine of lac. , perh. by error for a-jatya, itself either error, or with MIndic a for ā, for Skt. a-jātya (= Pali a-jacca); or else (perhaps more likely) error for a-janya, q.v.; ignoble (person): (na mleccheṣu na pāpakuleṣu naurabhrikeṣu [text noratrikeṣu]) na kaukkuṭikeṣu na jatyeṣu pratyājāyante.

, (1) or janā (birth, Skt. (mss., em. ˚kṣatriya), n. of a former Buddha:.
(otherwise only mother), woman (compares mātṛgrāma, q.v.): na saṃrarañje viṣamaṃ jananyām,, loved no woman wrongly.
, adj. ifc. (cf.; to Skt. janana, f. jananī), productive of …, producing: saṃvega-jananīyā kathā (prose); cf. Pali saṃvega-jananī (desanā).
(= Pali id.; and with var. ˚ṇam, disproved by Tib. and Pali), beauty (beautiful woman) of the country: = Tib. yul gyi bzaṅ mo (fem. suffix mo!); ˚ṇyā striyā sārdhaṃ paricaret; ˚ṇīṃ (=, text ˚ṇāṃ).
, m. (to janapada; representing stem ˚padin ?), countryman, man of the country: manuṣyā mahāmanuṣyā janapadayo mahājanapadayaḥ (prose), in long list of beings of all sorts.

, adj. or subst. m. (occurs, tho rarely, in Pali, e.g.; orig. prob. = jānant-, pres. pple., cf.; see next), knowing, wise (person): drakṣyanti jānu (all mss.; acc. sg.) imu saptapadāṃ kramantaṃ (vs); puruṣadhīreṇa puruṣajānena (nearly all mss.) (prose), by a wise one among men.

, in (prose) sarva-śreṣṭhi-naigamajānapatayaḥ, read ˚jānapadāḥ, people of the country. Tib. and Chin. lack this sentence.]

, text (vs) abhilāpo jānikaḥ, of whom is speech born? But read 'jāni, or better, m.c., ajāni (aor. pass.) kaḥ.]

, nt. (= Pali id.; nowhere else), knee-cap; knee; ˚lābhyāṃ (abl.) niścaritvā; in list of anuvyañjana, q.v., our, acc. to;, but the lists in and have a different reading which omits jānu; mostly used in a cliché, dakṣiṇaṃ (dakṣiṇa-;;; ubhau) jānumaṇḍalaṃ (˚le) pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpya; etc.;;;;;;;;.

(MIndic for Skt. jāmātṛ-ka, yām˚, rare for jāmātṛ; neither in Pali; AMg. jāmāuya), son-in-law: ˚tukasya; ˚tiko; all prose.
(muddy, from Skt. jambāla plus -a), n. of a man, hero of chap. 50:; etc.
(= jambuḍa, ˚ḍikā, qq.v.), a liquor-vessel: jāmbuḍī-sīdhum eva ca … baliṃ dadet (vs).
, adj. (= jambu˚, q.v.), of Jambudvīpa: ˚budvīpakāni ratnāni; usually of the people (manuṣya, sattva) of Jāmbudvīpa, jāmbu˚;;;;; jāmbū˚;;. All prose.

, (prose), or Jāmbūnadābhāsa, (vs), n. of a future Buddha, to be an incarnation of Mahākātyāyana.

= Skt. jayate, ˚ti (), conquers: nāśūro [Page242-a] jāyate senāṃ … śūras tu jāyate senām and 13 (vs, but in the fourth syllable of anuṣṭubh pādas ā can hardly be m.c.). The mg. is certain; no v.l. recorded.

, n. of a Tathāgata (living in Jāyā):.

, nt., prob. bouquet of flowers (here withered ones, to be removed from caityas); so jālaka is used in Skt.; the only plausible alternative would be spider-web, which jāla also means in Skt. (cf.) and Pali. In any case it means something the removal of which from caityas is a work of merit: yo jālakāni apanaye (so read with v.l. for upanaye) cetiyeṣu; choretva jālaṃ jinacetiyeṣu, repeated in the sequel; parallel choritva jālaṃ; apanīya (ed. em. upa˚) jālaṃ. (f. to jālin, q.v., but in sense of ensnaring or the like: = Pali id., ep. of taṇhā, with or without that word; the comms. have various explanations, three being offered on alone), perhaps ensnaring, or subst. enchantress, as ep. of tṛṣnā, thirst, longing: tasiṇāṃ ca jālinīṃ (vs); jālinīṃ tṛṣṇāṃ; tṛṣṇāṃ chittvāna jālinīṃ; jālinī … tṛṣṇā = Pali jālinī … taṇhā; without the word tṛṣṇā, Dharmasamuccaya (unpublished BHS work), acc. to; in a personal letter of May 16, 1945, kindly informs me that here jālinī ‘a ni plus ni moins le sens de ṭṛṣṇā, hors de toute ambiance métaphorique; de même pour viśālā’ (q.v.). We should, then, doubtless recognize the same [Page242-b] mg. in: sarvakileśabandhanalatāṃ … jālinīṃ (Tib. dra ba, net) (vs), and: iha jālinī … ṣaṭtriṃśaticāriṇī (vs), thirst which acts in 32 ways (as does taṇhā in Pali, s.v.); le filet dʼillusion. Most mss. and Calc. read indrajālinī for iha j˚ (hence ʼs rendering); but this is metr. impossible, and the epithet proves that tṛṣṇā is referred to.
, n. of a Bodhisattva:. Tib. renders jālinī by dra ba, net, or dra ba can, having a net. Perhaps having seductive (alluring) splendor? See s.v. jālinī, which otherwise = tṛṣṇā.

(should be ppp. of desid. of han-! but in mg. = jighatsita!), clearly means hungry in ˚ta-pipāsitasya kruddhasya kālakriyā; so Tib. bkres śiṅ skom pa, hungry and thirsty; and so translates, without any note, tho a note is surely needed! (cf. Skt. ˚na, nt., and jijñāsā, f.; perh. a blend of these two), test, trial: yūyaṃ kanyakā (Māra speaks to his daughters) … bodhisattvasya jijñāsanāṃ (no v.l.) kuruta (prose).

, apparently interj. or particle, chiefly in phrase: api hi jitaṃ;;;; this seems to be an expression of astonishment, something like Whoʼd have thought it? That beats all! Once, in, jitaṃ (v.l. jidaṃ) occurs by itself; the daughters of Māra, reporting to Māra, say: (any other man than the Bodhisattva, seeing us,) so jitaṃ mūrchitvā prapatiṣyad vā … cittakṣayaṃ vā prāpuṇe (but the Bodhisattva was unmoved); here too astonishment might be the connotation of the particle; he, good heavens! would have fallen down fainting …, or lost his wits. No etymology is apparent for the word.

, conqueror, standard epithet of a Buddha, so used in Skt.: = Tib. rgyal ba, victorious; et passim. The word appears to be used of any head, or at least founder, of a religious sect; see s.v. jina-śrāvaka.)

(corresponds to Pali Janesabha, Janavasabha; but the temptation to emend to Janarṣabha should prob. be resisted; Chin. versions on support Jina-), in, n. of a yakṣa; in n. of a prince, son of Vaiśravaṇa (Kubera), who dwelt in Tukhāra, ‘attended by (a) crore(s) of yakṣas’.
, n. of a former Buddha:. (Would be ˚varot˚ in Skt.)

, adj. (in these senses recorded nowhere else; Skt., Pali jimha, and Pkt. jimha, jimma, regularly crooked or fig. dishonest), (1) bereft of light, obscured, not shining, dull; regularly said of entities regarded as brightly shining in themselves, but having their light eclipsed or obscured by a greater radiance, esp. that emitted or caused by the Buddha; so at the bodhi-tree Buddha causes a radiance which makes the divine abodes of the gods jihma or jihmavarṇa; and by ʼs em. (for mss. jihmabala);;; (in all these jihma-bala might stand, of obscured, dulled power); similarly, jihma vipaśyatha (so divide) divya ātmabhāvāṃ (vs; Apsarases speak, looking at Māyāʼs superior beauty), see how (our) divine bodies are eclipsed (in splendor); jihma sarvatuṣitālayo bhuto (m.c. for bhūto) (vs), the whole abode of the Tuṣita became splendorless; sarvāṇi mārabhavanāni karonti jihmā (vs); jihma (so divide; acc. sg.) kurvati jagat sadevakam (vs); also fig. of the intelligence and senses; vijñāna, in (vs) ye gṛddhā lābhasatkāre jihma-vijñāna-(dull intelligence)-niśritā; and (apāyeṣūpapanno) durgandho bhavati jihmendriyo bhavaty avyaktendriyaḥ, … of dull and obscure (see avyakta) senses; (2) (cf. jihmīkṛtaḥ, below s.v. jihmīkaroti, with Tib.) disappointed, depressed, saddened, despondent: in (vs) read (with v.l.) jihmā-jihma (n. pl., āmreḍita) sudurmanā, very depressed and downcast; confirmed by Tib. dman zhiṅ dman; prob. so, a-jihma in (prose) aśaṅko 'jihmo, free from doubt and despondency (in a description of a Bodhisattva); to be sure the next words are 'śaṭho 'māyāvī, which suggest the Skt. meaning, not deceitful, but these lists of characteristics are apt to go in pairs, and aśaṅka suggests this BHS meaning of (a-)jihma, which is otherwise known [Page243-b] and easily develops from mg (1). , adj. (= next), obscuring: in Candrasūrya-jihmīkara-prabha, q.v. (having a splendor that obscures the moon and sun): (prose). But v.l. ˚karaṇa, which, being much commoner (I have noted no other case of ˚kara), is very likely the true reading.

, adj. (from next, with -ana), (1) obscuring, making (what is normally bright seem) dark or dull: candrasūryajihmīkaraṇayā prabhayā; indusūrya-jihmīkaraṇa-prabho; see also prec.; -tā, (jāmbūnada-suvarṇālaṃkāra-bhūtaṃ) saṃskṛtāvacara-kuśalamūlopacaya-jihmīkaraṇa-tayā, (it is like an ornament of finest gold) because it obscures (over-shadows, makes seem dull) things in the realm (see avacara) of the conditioned thru the acquisition of roots of merit; (2) disappointing (lit. darkening, so making despondent or the like), in a-ji˚, not disappointing (beggars): (upasaṃkrāntānāṃ, sc. yācanakānāṃ, cāvi) mānanājihmīkaraṇāvikṣepaṃ (adv.), while not showing disrespect to (beggars) who come to him, not disappointing them, and not turning them away; yācanaka-maitrīkāruṇyapūrvaṃgamasaṃprekṣaṇājihmīkaraṇa-, looking upon beggars with love and compassion and not disappointing them.

The identity of the two words can hardly be questioned. The [Page252-a] mg. of Pali tādi(n) is also quite clear, such (= tādṛś); doubt remains only as to whether this meant originally such as the Buddha, of the same quality as He, or such as a religious man ought to be, thus holy, following the path of true religion. On the Pali see esp. s.v., also on, where BHS uses evaṃrūpa in nearly the same sense; points out that tathārūpa glosses tādi in Acc. to tādi is usually applied to holy men, only rarely to Buddha. In BHS tāyin most often applies to Buddhas, but also fairly often to Bodhisattvas, and occasionally to other holy men. Once, at least, tādṛśaka, q.v., is clearly applied to a Buddha, like tāyin. These facts all together make it seem clear to me that the etym. and original mg. are as stated above. It is true that Tib. (see on below) interprets tāyin as if for trāyin, rendering protector or the like; some modern scholars (, on vs 73 of Chap. 1; ‘wohl nur fehlerhaft für trāyin’) assume that this was the etym. and primary mg. of tāyin.
